title: Choose Apogee's visual world
question: The roll dealt Ephemeris: the Hill chart drawn as an astronomer's altitude track. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Ephemeris
options.lineage: Almanac altitude tables and rise–culmination–set charts
options.thesis: Each Hill chart is an altitude track: a Scope rises, culminates at the apogee, and sets into done.
materials: Läge ticks every 10 like hour marks
spectral Läge ramp: violet → azure → green
options.viewport: Deep-indigo rail with Funktionsområden; the Projekt's hill fills the work area on a cool white ground, each Scope a coloured body trailing a dotted track of its recent Läge; a Scope list with Läge and Ägare beside it.
options.risk: Leans on the Apogee name; if the trails and ticks are overdone it turns into a space costume.

raised.raise: Start and Funktionsområde pages pack every Projekt as a stamp-size live hill thumbnail in a whole-cell grid, no stats.
Every rule, tick and axis is drawn at one device pixel in three ink values only.
The Läge 0–100 grid is a visible armature, ticks every 10, toggleable as a real state.
Dragging one Scope drives everything live: its colour, Läge readout, list row and trail update as you move.
Neutrals are a strict token scale; colour appears only where it carries Läge or state.

options.label: Orienteringskarta
options.lineage: ISOM orienteering maps and control description sheets
options.thesis: The hill as terrain every Swede has run: Scopes are purple control circles, and Läge colour is how runnable the ground is.
materials: ISOM terrain bands under the hill
options.viewport: White shell with a brown-contour hill profile; terrain bands under it run olive thicket (uphill) to yellow open land (downhill); numbered purple control circles mark Scopes; the Scope list is a control-description table.
options.case: Wins audience identification outright (it also topped my own grounded list as Swedish terrain maps); holds even on clarity, since the profile and circles read as plainly as Ephemeris.
options.risk: Läge colour is the terrain, not the dot; purple circles all match, so the scale reads only from the ground beneath them.

options.label: Convention circle catalog
options.thesis: Every Projekt a stamp-size cell in a numbered hall grid.
options.viewport: Packed thumbnail grid keyed to a hall map.
options.risk: No one in the organization identifies with it.
options.case: Loses both axes: foreign to the audience and the Hill chart gets lost in the grid.
options.kept: Whole-cell packing: every Projekt shown as its own tiny hill.

options.label: Centre-rail reference setting
options.thesis: A ruling engine draws every hairline at one device pixel.
options.viewport: Two text columns around a rail of keys.
options.risk: A book page, not a chart tool.
options.case: Loses both axes: reads as an edition, and text columns bury the hill.
options.kept: One-device-pixel rules in three ink values.

options.label: Monochrome product marketing
options.thesis: One neutral scale, one accent, proof beside every claim.
options.risk: Exactly the generic SaaS look you ruled out.
options.case: Loses both axes: it is the template the brief rejects.

options.label: Crouwel grid specimen
options.thesis: The construction grid is the design.
options.risk: A poster, not a working screen.
options.case: Loses both axes: no audience tie, and display letterforms compete with the chart.
options.kept: The Läge grid as a visible, toggleable armature.

options.label: Variable font specimen
options.thesis: One slider remaps the whole page live.
options.viewport: A giant glyph and a breathing grid.
options.kept: One drag drives every dependent readout live.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS project tool: sidebar, white cards, one blue accent, the hill as a grey curve with dots.
canonCard.viewport: Left sidebar, breadcrumb header, hill chart in a card, Scope table below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every project tool by design; close to the generic SaaS look you ruled out.
